newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says fire at Wilmington, Ca alkylation unit.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says fire at Wilmington, Ca alkylation unit.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Monday that it had a fire at the alkylation unit at its Wilmington, California plant near Los Angeles which has reduced the capacity of the plant.

"At 1215 a.m. Pacific time (1515 EST/1015 GMT) there was a fire on the alkylation unit at Texaco's refinery in Wilmington. Company fire department personnel responded and had the assistance of city and county fire department officials," said Phil Blackburn, a Texaco official.
He said the fire was not completely extinguished by shortly after 0900 EST. An investigation had been launched into the cause of the fire, the second at the plant in the past two months.

The plant, which has a crude distillation capacity of just under 92,000 barrels per day (bpd), had a fire at its 20,000 bpd hydrotreating unit in November. Blackburn said the investigation into that fire was still going on.
The alkylation unit is the smallest at the plant at around 9,000 bpd but Blackburn declined to say what the overall effect on the plant's capacity was.

"The plant will continue operation," he said, adding that there was no reason to believe that local environmental or other authorities would seek to shut the plant pending an investigation of the two fires.
"We had no injuries. Emissions were monitored and no harmful level of emissions escaped," he said.
